changes.summary: Rubric established: 6 weighted components, 2-floor comp gate, level/location gates, risk penalty, and a two-layer predicted-vs-observed split.

Added an outcome-status vocabulary and a channel field. The first retrospective's predicted change - raise the warm-path weight - turned out to be unsupported: every application to date had come through one channel, so no contrast group existed.

Replaced a 2-tier location gate with 4 tiers and made it a ranking tiebreak rather than a gate. Logged even though it was already applied, because an unlogged change is invisible to the next retrospective.

Added a second independent axis for attainability, because the original score measured desirability-if-obtained and had no attainability term. Labelled ordinal, not a probability, until it has outcome validation.

A seniority prefix on an internal posting is a naming quirk, not a level signal. Re-scoring was done by a tested function rather than by hand, which exposed a small calibration residual that was reported rather than smoothed.

Added an internal-transfer channel value. Without it, thirteen internal applications would have been recorded under the wrong channel - the same mis-recording the channel field was introduced to prevent.
Documented that two similarly-named inputs answer different questions, and gave one of them a numeric scale for the first time. It had carried none since the rubric was established.

An ambiguous compensation test was resolved to a single defined reading. The prior phrasing gave two defensible, opposite answers on the same live role, one of which would have silently discarded a role being actively pursued.

Added a years-of-experience gate after the top-ranked role turned out to require twice the tolerance. Title was explicitly rejected as a gate: it mispredicted in both directions. Years are read only after a qualifications heading, because one posting mentions an unrelated 18-year span in a founder biography.

reasons: The favourable arm was effectively a single organisation, so it was one data point wearing the costume of two.
Predicted fit ran inverse to observed outcomes, but the relationship was fully confounded by application channel.
Most channel data had never been recorded at all, so the contrast the tuning depended on did not exist yet.
whyNoTuning.rule: Capture before tuning. A weight only moves on evidence that could have moved it the other way.
